name: Rundfunk- und Radiomuseum Innsbruck
kurzbeschreibung: The Radiomuseum in Innsbruck: a fascinating journey through 100 years of broadcasting technology featuring over 400 operational historic radios and phonographs.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Rundfunk- und Radiomuseum Innsbruck is located in the easily accessible Pradl district of the Tyrolean provincial capital Innsbruck at Heinzenbichl 2, at an altitude of around 580 metres. Founded and run on a voluntary basis by passionate broadcasting technicians and collectors, this technology museum houses one of the most comprehensive and valuable collections of historic audio and broadcasting equipment in all of Austria. Across several exhibition floors, the museum presents more than 400 operational original exhibits spanning over a century of media history ? from the very first faint radio signals of the 1920s to the era of modern transistor radios.

100 Years of Radio History & Rarities

The exhibition takes visitors on an acoustic and visual journey back to the era when radio was humanity's first electronic mass medium. Among the oldest and most precious treasures are historic Edison-Phonographen with wax cylinders dating from around 1900, hand-cranked gramophones with magnificent horns, and early crystal radio receivers from the 1920s, which operated without any mains electricity using only headphones. Arranged chronologically, these are followed by elegant wooden cathedral radios of the 1930s, Volksempf?nger, historic post-war tube radios, as well as early television sets and tape recorders from renowned manufacturers such as Minerva, Ingelen, Kapsch, Telefunken, and Philips. A special highlight of the museum is the fully functional historic radio workshop: here, technicians demonstrate how thermionic tubes, variable capacitors, and measuring instruments work. Visitors can experience first-hand how vintage vacuum tube radios slowly begin to glow after being switched on, filling the room with the distinctively warm tube sound of days gone by.

Visit & Getting There

The Radiomuseum Innsbruck is open to visitors year-round on selected days: Wednesdays from 14:00 to 17:00 and Saturdays from 10:00 to 13:00 (closed on public holidays; special guided tours for groups, school classes, and technology enthusiasts are available at any time upon request). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. ?6.00, seniors and students approx. ?5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. ?3.00, young children free. Holders of the all-inclusive Innsbruck Card enjoy free admission. Getting there by public transport: from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof take tram line 3 or bus line C to the Pradler Platz or Leipziger Platz stop (only about a three-minute walk). By car: motorway A12 (exit Innsbruck Ost), parking is available in the surrounding short-term parking zones.

Tips

The exhibition rooms of the Radiomuseum are largely accessible via an elevator; the museum team is gladly available to assist visitors with limited mobility. A highlight for visitors is the demonstration of historic shellac records on an original gramophone from 1910. Technology enthusiasts can browse through vintage schematics and radio magazines from the 1920s to the 1960s in the reference library.
